articles.title: World shares rise after technology shares advance on Wall Street ahead of US inflation data
articles.description: Global markets are higher after U.S. stocks rallied from last week’s losses. U.S. futures edged higher and oil prices fell. European markets rose in early trading and Asian stocks were boosted by gains in AI-related sectors. China reported its trade surplus for 2026 has already surpassed $1 trillion. Investors are watching for U.S. inflation data for October. On Monday, the S&P 500 jumped 2.3%, the Dow Jones Industrial Average gained 2.2%, and the Nasdaq composite rose 2.7%. Stocks were lifted by a decline in the price of Brent crude, after President Donald Trump said a resumption of strikes on Iran is “highly unlikely” if the United States sees progress in negotiations toward ending the war.
articles.content:
HONG KONG (AP) — Global markets were higher Tuesday after U.S. stocks rallied, recovering most of their big losses from last week, while investors awaited U.S. inflation data for October.
